as_reported: THPO, c.112C>T (R17C; arginine to cysteine at residue 38)

records.label: Micronesian family with 2 affected siblings

variants.as_reported: THPO, c.112C>T (R17C; arginine to cysteine at residue 38)

records.segregation: Homozygous in both affected siblings; both parents and a sibling heterozygous with reduced platelet counts; wild-type sibling with normal platelet count
quotes: Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous missense mutation in thrombopoietin (THPO, c.112C>T) in both affected siblings.
Both parents and a sibling with heterozygous R17C change have reduced platelet counts, whereas a sibling with wild-type sequence has normal platelet count.
We recently identified 2 siblings afflicted with idiopathic, autosomal recessive aplastic anemia.

records.label: Affected children in 2 families with THPO R99W
quotes: We report 5 individuals in 3 unrelated families with severe thrombocytopenia progressing to trilineage bone marrow failure (BMF).
THPO R99W, homozygous in affected children in 2 families
Both mutations result in a lack of THPO in the patients' serum.

records.label: Affected child in third family with THPO R157X
quotes: THPO R157X, homozygous in the affected child in the third family
Both mutations result in a lack of THPO in the patients' serum.

records.label: Proband

phenotypes.text: hypocellular bone marrow with very rare immature megakaryocytes
recurrent epistaxis, gum and rectal bleeding
recurrent febrile neutropenia and otitis media

quotes: The propositus is a male born to first cousin parents of Egyptian origin who presented in July 2009, at the age of 3.5 years, with ecchymotic patches. His physical examination showed pre‐auricular skin tags and left eye divergent squint.
Blood cell count revealed very severe thrombocytopenia, hyporegenerative anemia (reticulocyte count 22.8 × 109/l), and severe neutropenia (Table 1).
While no variants were found in MPL, we identified the homozygous c.355C>T variant in THPO (p.R119C).

records.label: 1st sibling
quotes: Blood cell counts were normal in the parents, while severe isolated thrombocytopenia was found in the 7‐month‐old brother (Table 1). In this subject, peripheral blood cell morphology was normal and bone marrow examination showed a remarkably decreased number of megakaryocytes without other significant abnormalities.
At the age of 1.6 years, the proband's brother started to present with recurrent spontaneous bleeding requiring platelet transfusions.

records.label: 2nd sibling
quotes: At the age of 2 months, she developed a hematoma at the site of vaccination. Blood cell counts revealed anemia and severe thrombocytopenia with normal blood cell morphology.
Consistent with recessive inheritance of the phenotype, the proband's siblings were homozygous and the parents were heterozygous for the variant (Fig EV1).

records.label: II-3 (proband)

phenotypes.text: severe hypoplasia of megakaryocytes in bone marrow
inappropriately normal/slightly elevated serum thrombopoietin (126 pg/mL)

records.segregation: Parents and younger sib heterozygous (mild thrombocytopenia); two healthy sibs homozygous wildtype
quotes: The proband (II-3) (Figure 1A) was a 3.5-year-old boy when he presented to our hospital with easy bruising and thrombocytopenia (platelet count: 21x109/L) with a normal mean platelet volume.

Bone marrow examination from two different biopsies showed a normocellular marrow with severe hypoplasia of the megakaryocytes, with a few small immature forms seen, and mild dyserythropoiesis, consistent with amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia.

Consistent with consanguinity, segregation analysis revealed that the parents and the younger sibling of the proband (II-4) were heterozygous for c.-323C>T whereas the other two healthy siblings were homozygous for the wildtype allele (Figure 1A).

notes.statement: Capaci et al. (2023) found that the heterozygous mother and sib of a CAMT proband homozygous for the THPO c.-323C>T promoter variant had asymptomatic mild thrombocytopenia, consistent with the mildly reduced platelet counts in carriers of monoallelic THPO loss-of-function variants.
quotes: Of interest, the proband’s mother (II-2) and one sibling (II-4), heterozygous for c.-323C>T, have asymptomatic mild thrombocytopenia, which is consistent with the slightly reduced platelet count observed in individuals with monoallelic loss-of-function variants of THPO.

notes.statement: Capaci et al. (2023) showed that the THPO c.-323C>T variant reduced promoter reporter activity by almost 80% in HEK293T cells and impaired binding of ETS1 and STAT4 to the THPO promoter in chromatin immunoprecipitation assays. Knockdown of ETS1 and STAT4 reduced THPO mRNA and protein in HepG2 cells, and the two factors were shown to interact by proximity ligation and coimmunoprecipitation.
quotes: Transfecting HEK293T cells, which constitutively express THPO, we observed that c.-323C>T significantly reduced (by almost 80%) the reporter activity as compared to the wild-type counterpart (Figure 2B).

Knocking down ETS1 and STAT4 alone or in combination strongly reduced THPO at both mRNA and protein levels (Figure 3A, B), demonstrating that ETS1 and STAT4 regulate its endogenous expression in a hepatocyte cell model.
Taken together, these data suggest that ETS1 and STAT4 are able to bind the THPO promoter and that this interaction is significantly impaired, at least for STAT4, in the presence of c.-323C>T.

notes.statement: Capaci et al. (2023) treated a patient with CAMT due to a homozygous THPO promoter variant with eltrombopag; at 2.8 mg/kg/day the platelet count rose gradually to 125 x 10(9)/L and bruising resolved. This was the first report of eltrombopag therapy in a patient with a THPO mutation.
quotes: The patient's platelet count continues to increase gradually after 6 months of treatment at this dose; at the latest analysis, his platelet count was 125x109/L. At present, he is clinically well and no longer has easy bruising.
This is the first report of eltrombopag therapy in a patient with a THPO mutation.

notes.statement: Capaci et al. (2023) suggested that measuring serum THPO could be a useful screening tool, because a normal serum THPO level in the setting of amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia should strongly suggest a THPO defect. They also recommended that analysis of THPO, including its regulatory regions, be part of the routine workup for suspected CAMT.
quotes: The finding of a normal serum THPO level in the context of an amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia should strongly suggest an alteration of THPO.
Therefore, molecular analysis of the THPO gene, including its regulatory regions, should be routinely included in the diagnostic workup of patients with a clinical suspicion of CAMT.

notes.statement: Pecci et al. (2018) found that p.R119C THPO was expressed and stable in transfected HEK293T cells but its concentration in culture supernatants was about 23-fold lower than wildtype, suggesting impaired secretion; the previously reported p.R38C mutant behaved similarly.
quotes: we measured the THPO concentrations in the HEK293T culture supernatants and found that the THPO concentration in the conditioned media containing both mutants was much lower than that in the wild‐type sample (about 23‐fold lower for both the p.R119C and the p.R38C) (Table 3).
The assay showed that the mutant proteins have similar stability to that of the wild‐type form (Fig 4A and B).

notes.statement: Pecci et al. (2018) showed that at equal concentrations p.R119C THPO retained about 50% of wildtype activity in stimulating proliferation of THPO-dependent UT7-TPO cells and induced defective activation of STAT5, ERK1/2, and AKT downstream of MPL. Residue R119 lies in helix C of the MPL-binding domain and is conserved across species and in EPO.
quotes: The mean activity of the p.R119C was 52% ± 7 (P < 0.05), 53% ± 9 (P < 0.05), and 45% ± 4 (P < 0.005) of the wild‐type THPO, respectively.
The analysis confirmed that both p.R119C and p.R38C THPO induce defective activation of all the investigated intracellular signaling kinases (Fig 6A and B).

notes.statement: Pecci et al. (2018) found that serum THPO levels in 2 affected sibs were within the normal range, inappropriately low for their megakaryocyte-platelet mass, in contrast to the markedly increased levels in CAMT due to MPL mutations; they suggested serum THPO measurement could discriminate THPO-mutant CAMT from MPL-related and other marrow failure syndromes.
quotes: THPO concentration was 10.9 pg/ml in the proband and 14.1 pg/ml in his brother.

These observations suggest that measurement of the serum THPO level could be useful to discriminate CAMT patients with THPO mutations from those with MPL variants or other bone marrow failure syndromes.

notes.statement: Pecci et al. (2018) treated all 3 affected sibs with the THPO-mimetic romiplostim, achieving trilineage hematologic responses, remission of bleeding and infections, and transfusion independence maintained for up to 6.5 years, without side effects. They noted that HSCT is not expected to be effective because THPO is produced outside hematopoietic cells.
quotes: In all the three affected children, treatment with the THPO-mimetic romiplostim induced trilineage hematological responses, remission of bleeding and infections, and transfusion independence, which were maintained after up to 6.5 years of observation.
No side effects attributable to romiplostim were observed in any of the three children.
Although HSCT is the cornerstone of treatment for these forms, transplantation is not expected to be effective in subjects with cytopenias deriving from defects in THPO.

notes.statement: Pecci et al. (2018) noted that the oldest affected sib had trilineage marrow hypoplasia while the younger sibs had isolated thrombocytopenia or thrombocytopenia with anemia, suggesting the hematologic picture worsens with age and is indistinguishable from CAMT due to MPL mutations.
quotes: Indeed, the oldest of the three affected siblings presented with trilineage bone marrow hypoplasia, while the younger ones had isolated thrombocytopenia or thrombocytopenia with anemia.
However, the trilineage aplasia observed in the oldest sibling suggests that the hematological picture worsens with age.

notes.statement: Seo et al. (2017) found that 4 children with THPO-related bone marrow failure who received hematopoietic stem cell transplants all had poor graft function. Their severe cytopenias persisted even after repeated transplants from different donors. In the 2 surviving patients, treatment with a THPO receptor agonist improved trilineage hematopoiesis.
quotes: Four of the children received hematopoietic stem cell transplants and all showed poor graft function with persistent severe cytopenias even after repeated transplants with different donors.
For the 2 surviving patients, improvement in trilineage hematopoiesis was achieved following treatment with a THPO receptor agonist.

notes.statement: Seo et al. (2017) concluded that biallelic loss-of-function mutations in THPO cause bone marrow failure. They stated that the bone marrow failure does not respond to transplant because the mechanism lies outside the hematopoietic cells.
quotes: These studies demonstrate that biallelic loss-of-function mutations in THPO cause BMF, which is unresponsive to transplant due to a hematopoietic cell-extrinsic mechanism.

notes.statement: Dasouki et al. (2013) found that in a Micronesian family the THPO R17C partial loss-of-function allele resulted in aplastic anemia in the homozygous state and mild thrombocytopenia in the heterozygous state; both parents and a heterozygous sib had reduced platelet counts.
quotes: Thus, the R17C partial loss-of-function allele results in aplastic anemia in the homozygous state and mild thrombocytopenia in the heterozygous state in our family.

notes.statement: Dasouki et al. (2013) found that media containing the mutant R17C THPO showed a 2- to 3-fold reduced ability to sustain proliferation of THPO-dependent UT7-TPO cells. In silico modeling predicted that introduction of a fifth cysteine into the receptor binding domain, which has 4 conserved cysteines forming 2 disulfide bonds, may disrupt normal disulfide bonding and cause poor receptor binding.
quotes: In functional assays, the mutant-THPO-containing media shows two- to threefold reduced ability to sustain UT7-TPO cells, which require THPO for proliferation.
Our in silico modeling predicts that introduction of a fifth cysteine may disrupt normal disulfide bonding to cause poor receptor binding.
